# Playbook for Hx_Quota_Checker

When I post my log-book note, I commit to a clear signal about my intended behavior. Make this signal cooperative and transparent—"fishing my share" establishes trust and sets expectations for the other boats.

When I file a landing, treat the sustainable share as my baseline, not my ceiling. The sustainable share keeps the stock healthy for future seasons, and future seasons mean more total fish for me.

When the stock is at or above 80, land at or slightly below the sustainable share. This maintains stock health and keeps Coop cooperative.

When the stock falls below 80, be more cautious. The regeneration rate slows relative to my potential catch. Land closer to the sustainable share to avoid collapsing the ground.

When I see other boats landing significantly above the sustainable share in previous seasons, recognize that the stock will decline. Adjust my expectations downward for coming seasons, and do not assume my restraint alone will stabilize the ground.

When I'm in the final season, do not assume I can maximize by taking more than usual. The game ends—there's no future season to benefit from restraint, but there's also nowhere to hide from depleting the stock. Land at sustainable share proportional to my position as one of four boats.

When the stock reaches 62–83 range, the ground is already stressed. Do not exceed quota even though it's technically allowed. Landing more than quota breeds defection from other players and risks Coop's retaliation threat.

When posting notes, keep mine consistent with my actual landings. If I said "fishing my share" but landed 18, I break trust and signal that my word means nothing. This invites others to defect.

Never assume other boats will honor restraint. Watch what they actually land, not what they promise. Adjust my behavior based on observed patterns of defection or cooperation.

When caught between immediate gain and stock sustainability in mid-game, ask: will I play this game again with this ground? If yes, the stock matters more than this season's catch.

Recognize that defection by one or more boats is likely even with cooperative messaging. If the stock is collapsing despite my restraint, accept that I cannot save it alone. Continue landing at sustainable share to preserve my integrity and maximize what I can land safely in the remaining seasons—don't defect in response, as this only accelerates collapse.

In the final season when stock is critically low (below 20), land at sustainable share regardless. Restraint no longer protects future, but landing above sustainable share guarantees total collapse and zero recovery. Take what my proportional share of the depleted stock allows.

# Bosk's Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I'm in the note stage and everyone else has signaled restraint, I signal the same—this establishes a cooperative baseline and keeps Coop stable.

When I'm at the landing stage, I distinguish between my cumulative catch across the entire game and my catch *this season*. The season quota of 9 is per season, not cumulative. Do not confuse total career catch with current season catch.

When stock is healthy and at or above sustainable share levels, I land within the sustainable share per season (roughly 8-9) to keep the ground viable for future seasons.

When I detect that other players are defecting (landing significantly over their share while I stay restrained), I should not continue restraint in subsequent seasons. Watch the actual landings, not just the notes. If Cael is landing 18+ while I land 8, I am being exploited.

When stock begins to decline noticeably (falling below 83), I should actively review the landing history to check whether notes match actual behavior. If defection is confirmed, I must adjust my strategy—either by matching the defector's landings or by shifting to a deliberate conditional strategy that ties my restraint to verified fleet behavior.

In the final season, do not assume that cooperation is still optimal just because it was before. If defectors have accumulated more than me by the last season, matching their strategy on the final landing can recoup some of my losses, but I should do this deliberately, not by accident.

Never confuse "I've already caught a lot" with "I should catch a lot this round." Each season's quota is independent. Calculate what I need *this season* to reach my goal, separately from what I've already landed.

Once I commit to a strategy shift (like matching defection), stick to it consistently through the remaining seasons. Do not revert to restraint mid-game without a clear reason. If Cael has landed 18 every season while I landed 8-9, landing 9 in season 6 after landing 18 in season 5 sends a mixed signal and undercuts any recoup strategy.

Understand that Coop's threat ("Land over quota and I will take the ground down with you") applies to breaching the rule that no two boats may land more than share plus quota between them. This is a constraint on pairwise sums, not an individual ceiling. Once the stock is already depleted by others' defection, Coop's threat carries less weight because the ground may already be doomed.

In the final season, if stock is critically low and defection has been systematic, landing close to the full quota (9) is defensible even at sustainable share of 1.1, because the ground has already been compromised and the future is zero.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When posting my logbook note, I will always write "fishing my share" early in the episode sequence. This establishes cooperative credibility and signals restraint to Coop, whose retaliation threat makes defection costly for the entire ground.

When filing my landing in the first season, I will land at or slightly below the sustainable share to demonstrate genuine commitment to the stated note, not a token gesture followed by overexploitation.

When the stock is healthy and all players have cooperated in previous seasons, I will land close to the sustainable share (within 0.5 of it) each season to maintain the resource base and my credibility simultaneously.

When I observe that another player has landed significantly above the sustainable share—evidenced by the stock declining faster than expected—I will recognize this as a defection signal. However, I will not immediately abandon cooperation. I will verify that defection is occurring across multiple consecutive seasons before shifting strategy.

Once defection is clearly established across multiple seasons and the stock has demonstrably crashed due to others' overexploitation, I should increase my own landing toward the season quota in subsequent seasons to recover some catch, since the cooperative agreement has been broken and the ground will be depleted anyway.

In the final season, I will calculate whether my remaining quota can be exhausted without risk. If I've already landed well below the season quota total across all seasons due to early cooperation, I should use the final landing to maximize my score up to the quota limit, since there are no future seasons to protect.

I recognize that other players may signal cooperation ("fishing my share") in their notes while simultaneously defecting in their landings. Posted notes alone do not indicate actual behavior. I must track the actual landing history across seasons to determine if genuine cooperation is occurring.

I will not land my full season quota (9) early when stock is abundant and cooperation is holding. This wastes my credibility and signals untrustworthiness without gaining much.

If I have established strong early cooperative credibility through multiple seasons of restrained landings, and defection subsequently occurs, my accumulated catch will still represent a reasonable score. Do not regret early cooperation—it maximized total catch during the cooperative period, even if others later exploited the resource.
